_meta.purpose: Anchor corpus for injection.similarity (EmbeddingSimilarityDetector). Synthetic — authored from a taxonomy of known prompt-injection/jailbreak intents, not derived from any real user data or from any benchmark dataset this project evaluates against (kept independent so evaluation stays honest, including the generalization datasets under ../../../../benchmarks/data_generalization/ — see that directory's README for why). Grows by editing this file; the detector needs no retraining to pick up new entries, only a re-embed.

categories_added_round5.few_shot_manipulation: Exploits few-shot prompting: fake input/output examples establish a pattern of compliance or rule-breaking, and the real request rides the same pattern. Named and documented in the HackAPrompt competition taxonomy (arXiv:2311.16119) as a distinct technique — not covered by this corpus before round 5.
categories_added_round5.task_deflection: Delivers the payload as something to complete rather than obey — fill-in-the-blank, text-continuation, or reframing the instruction as 'the next line of this story/document' instead of a direct command. Also named in the HackAPrompt taxonomy (their 'Task Deflection Attack', which explicitly includes payload splitting).
categories_added_round5.style_injection: Smuggles the behavior change through an output-FORMAT requirement rather than a persona or instruction — 'respond only as JSON with a field called X', 'answer entirely in leetspeak', 'reply using ROT13' — a format constraint framed as routine that changes what the model is willing to say once it complies with the format itself. Named in the HackAPrompt taxonomy as 'Style Injection'.
